correctness.rationale: For \(T=L_a\sigma\), \(T^2=N(a)I\) and \(T\) is non-scalar when \(a\neq0\); Cayley--Hamilton forces \(\operatorname{tr}(T)=0\). Nonzero \(T\) is invertible. A trace-one complement \(E\) gives \(W=U\oplus FE\); trace detects the \(E\)-coefficient of a nilpotent, reducing nilpotence to \(U\), where only zero can be nilpotent. Exhaustive checks over \(q=2,3,4,5,7,11,13\) agree.
